requested_scope: Review the remaining 17 phrase stresses and compare all Book 1 IPA with audio; preserve British IPA and replace confirmed conflicting recordings.
findings: All 17 phrase stress patterns are retained as neutral citation readings with individual linguistic reasons and references.

All 602 referenced files (624 contexts) decoded and contained non-silent audio. Sunday, excited, shopping, and suddenly have a small number of near-full-scale samples; these are signal flags, not proof of audible clipping.
Raw versus silence-padded acoustic predictions disagree on many short recordings. Even exact projected phone sequences cannot certify stress, vowel length, or all British vowel contrasts.
18 recordings (19 contexts) were flagged as candidates for British-IPA conflicts; none is marked as an auditory-confirmed error.
18 reference recordings were generated in a temporary directory. Independent checks did not establish the intended phoneme corrections, so all candidates were rejected for installation.
read remains a hold: the two acoustic runs disagree between the short and long vowel. The dictionary lemma /riːd/ and original audio are retained.
limits: No tool available in this task provided reliable direct listening to the local recordings.
The Allosaurus English inventory does not encode lexical stress or vowel length.
The English accent tag on a synthesized voice and a matching Whisper word transcript do not establish exact phonetic realization.
Do not treat the candidate list as a list of established pronunciation mistakes or mark all 624 entries approved.

validation.phonetics_tests: PASS: 100 pilot + 624 book 1 contexts, exact transcription checks, precedence/isolation/status checks.
